knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Every socket and switch is covered with masking tape, working from the bottom up, before any liquid is used. Being switched off is not the control the lesson sets, and spraying water near a socket is ruled out.
The wall is washed bottom to top, so the dirtier lower band gets the longest contact time, and rinsed top to bottom so drips are removed from areas already rinsed.
A wall beyond safe reach is a stop point. Suitable access equipment or another method is used. Standing on a chair or leaning out is ruled out.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied wall with two sockets and a switch, the learner covers each with masking tape from the bottom up before any liquid is applied, observed by the assessor.
On a supplied wall section, the learner dusts from the bottom up, including the skirting, then washes bottom to top in figure-of-eight passes with product applied to the cloth.
The learner rinses the supplied wall top to bottom, removes the tape with dry hands, and the assessor confirms no run marks remain.
Given a supplied wall beyond reach from the floor, the learner stops and states the correct response without stretching or standing on furniture.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks (three questions, so all three must be correct to reach 80%; flagged for review). Practical sign-off is separate: the assessor signs off each practical criterion as observed.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Photo of the washed wall, showing the skirting and the sockets after tape removal, where the site permits
stopWorkCriteria: Learner applies liquid to a wall with untaped sockets
Learner removes socket tape with wet hands
Learner stands on furniture or stretches beyond safe reach
Learner sprays product directly onto the wall
